Hi Rebecca —

Thanks again for the great conversation last week. Based on usage growth you described (AI triage + expanded embeddings for search), I sketched a couple of paths that try to balance cost predictability with short-term capacity you need for the next 12 months. Key points:

- Option A: 18% uplift on current committed units to cover forecasted Q3 surge; co-term to 12/31/2028; 3% discount on committed over 12 months.
- Option B: staged top-up (6 month bridge) with a reserved-burst buffer and a 10% uplift converted to vouchers if not consumed.
- Tradeoffs: A simplifies billing and gives lower unit price; B preserves flexibility if growth flattens.

I've attached a draft proposal and the Q1 usage summary so your procurement/finance team can see the numbers that informed the uplift. Before I pull legal in, two asks:
1) Can procurement confirm whether co-term to calendar-year end is required?
2) Any internal discount approval thresholds (e.g., >15% needs VP approval)?

If helpful, Ben and Priyom can join a 30-min call next week to walk through the proposal and walk procurement through PO/timing.

Thanks —

All —

Thanks for the context. I ran the numbers and attached a compact comparison (SLA-exceptions-notes.txt with the high-level math). Summary:

- Year-end co-term (12/31/2028) gives ~14.8% blended uplift discount vs a quarter co-term because we can annualize the added committed units over 18 months; net ARR difference ~ $58k.
- Quarter co-term provides more flexibility for Clarity but the per-unit price is ~6% higher for the uplift portion.
- Voucher policy (for Option B): vouchers valid 9 months, rollover allowed up to 25% of voucher value once, then expire. Unused vouchers after 9 months convert to a one-time credit at 50% of face value (this preserves revenue protection while offering flexibility).
- Burst pool: we can offer a 10% burst reserve billed only when used at a 1.4x spot multiplier; any sustained use (>30 days in a rolling 60-day window) triggers an automatic review and proposed committed conversion.

Next steps I propose:
1) Naomi to present the numbers to Rebecca and procurement on 6/29 (09:30-10:00 PST) — Naomi, can you confirm?
2) Priyom to prepare a term-sheet snippet with the voucher clauses for legal.
3) Lauren to confirm discount approval threshold and invoice-credit feasibility (will update by 6/28).

Attached: SLA-exceptions-notes.txt (plain text, 4 KB) — includes the math and the example invoice for both co-term options.
